author: Dragunovi
content:
**New Priest Racial Spells (Updated 3rd of April 2025):**
The first spell they get is Grace of the Sunwell. Obtained at level 10, it is a targeted buff that increases the target's melee, ranged, and spellcasting speed by 10% for 10 seconds, with a 6 minute cooldown. Because the spell is entirely percentage based, it does not have any other ranks to learn.

The second spell they get is Sun's Embrace, first obtained at level 20, with further ranks available at 36, 48, and 60. Sun's Embrace is a self-targeted buff that reduces the mana cost of the next 5 Smite, Holy Fire, and Holy Nova spells you cast within 20 seconds by a flat amount, with a 5 minute cooldown.

Dwarf Priests now have Avatar instead of Fear Ward as the latter has been made baseline. Avatar increases your target's armor by 25% and all resistances by an amount equal to x1.5 of your level.

Elune's Grace has been removed for Night Elf Priests.
Night Elf Priests will now instead be able to use Bows with the ability to auto shoot and learn the ability Searing Shot at level 20.

author: Lily
content: For PvE you're going to want Spirit Tap - helps with leveling and has some occasional usage in niche situations. The next tier you want everything. 10% hit is lovely, and the uptime on SWP and less threat is ideal.  Mind Flay is obvious, and from what I hear you want around 4 points in improved MB to smooth your rotation. You want full Shadow Weaving, full range increase so MF's range isn't awful on some fights, and all of the Vampire talents because the health we bring and mana is super useful. The last shadow bits from be the straight shadow damage increase and shadow form. The rest of the points you stick into Disc looking to get  meditation and inner focus.

author: Greendam
content:
The concept of "leveling as shadow" or "leveling as Disc" are very misleading noob trap for priest because shadow priests don't get their full power until lvl 40, and many essential talents for Disc are actually in Holy tree.
2/2 wand spec and 5/5 spirit tap, then spend points in holy tree all the way to 5/5 spiritual guidance can make your smite out dmg wanding around lvl 30 and benefit your healing capacity at the same time.
After that, you can either spend points into Disc tree to further boost your smite damage or respec to shadow if you really want to at lvl 42 (you can at lvl 40 but you will lose 2/2 wand spec so I suggest to wait a little bit more)

author: DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde)
content:
your first 7 talent points you’re going to want to put into 2/2 Wand spec and 5/5 spirit tap basically regardless of your build. Spirit Tap greatly improves your mana efficiency and cuts down on drinking/eating. Wands do pretty good damage, massive actually at low lvls so 2/2 improves it even more, you’ll learn a wand is a Priests best friend while lvling. if you want to do a mix of dps and maybe healing for dungeons do your next 20/21 points into Holy and this will let you be Smite Dps or be a Healer for dungeons. 

I would do this until ~43.
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/priest?points=SoAAAAAAAAAAAAaQFCABAoAAAAAAFAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=

Shadow kinda sucks until lvl 44 and you get Rank 4 Mind Flay. So you can respec to Shadow if you’d like. If you wanna stay Smiting i’d either decide if you want to keep healing dungeons or continue to improve smite damage from here. If you wanna focus more on damage go down the disc tree to pick up Purifying Flames and Searing Light. If you want to improve your healing for dungeons, go back into the Holy Tree to pick up Spiritual Healing since it improves all your healing by 30%

author: DemonBoyJr (Tel’Abim-Horde)
content:
All you need to Lasher farm is 1 point in Holy Nova. Any standard Disc or Holy build should work. That being said you need to be able to cast ~9 Novas to kill a pack so ~6k mana. Tbh you don’t really need to PW:S on pre-pull on single packs if you’re just starting and meet the bare minimum mana requirement, but definitely helps on 2+ pack pulls when you start wanting to go faster.

This is your standard Disc Dps build. I wouldn’t make a Strict Lasher farm build since it’s kind of a waste of a Spec slot, but I suppose you could remove points from Searing Light/Purifying Flames to put points into Improved PW:S and Resurgent Shield to maximize your mana efficiency.

author: HolyScheiss
content:
Regarding the talent - you only need 1 talent point since you won`t be fighting against high lvl targets all the time.
3/3 talent gives you 6% spell hit, where the maximum spell  hit you need is 16%. That means you only need 10 spell hit from gear. Early leveling gear that has spell hit is very rare and I would say it is better to get spell power or stats , compared to spell hit for lvl-ing gear. 
@lvl 60, if you want to go in dungeons and raids - getting spell hit is a must (especially as much as possible to reach hit cap).

The 16% are for mobs that are 3+ levels above your level. But the formula is as follows:
Since all casters have an inherent 1% chance to miss always-
Mobs the same level as you, you have 4% chance to miss, so 3% is the cap you want
Mobs 1 level above you, you have a 5% chance to miss, so 4% is the cap you want
Mobs 2 levels above you, you have a 6% chance to miss, so 5% is the cap you want
Mobs 3+ levels above you, you have a (WHOPPING) 17% chance to miss, so 16% is the cap you want.

content:
Yes, in order to maximize their dps, the person receiving the chastise will set up a macro with a whisper : 
/w discpriest chastise me now!

The disc priest will set up a macro : 
/target partymembername
/cast chastise

Targets which are most favorable for Chastise are : 
Affliction Warlocks & Arcane Mages > 2H Melee DPS (Arms Warr, Melee Hunters, AP Rets, Enh Shamans) > Dual-Wield Melee (Fury warriors & Rogues) > everything else 
You can , of course, cast chastise on yourself, but the gains are limited compared to other classeses (we are on the bottom of the list).
Remember that you can cast chastise , if your target is above 80% health. So in some situations if you want to chastise, you might need to heal the target with a flash heal and then slap him.

It's more complicated than an assessment of its position in the numbers. Basically, 
- Shadow priests are indeed middle to low end in terms of dps.

- Ironically it provides lots of mana but is often mana starved as its spells have a big frontloaded cost..
- It doesnt scale with any stat but Spell power, Mind Flay and Shadow word pain cannot crit and are not affected by haste, meaning that all crit does is increase Mind Blast which is about 15% of the dps of the Priest, and haste does nothing. 
- Their only Aoe is Holy nova, which is trash since sets give Shadow Spell power not raw spell power and even if it wasnt trash, on a pack post-patch, their role is to apply %shadow damage to every target by SW:P on each target, which makes them boring and OOM.

They are in quite a high-demand since there are not a lot of them and they provide unique mana battery effect + %shadow damage + makes their party pretty much immune to slow damage but their design is a bit wonky as you might see in the history of this channel, full of priests begging for mindflay to be able to crit or for other QoL that just never come.

author: Pyronus
content:
Any raid leader who only judges healers by their healing done is wrong and you should not take them seriously. 
I think you can divide healing into two categories: Proactive and Reactive healing.

Reactive healing is where the raid takes damage and you try your best to top their health again.  The damage is done and now you're healing them.
Proactive healing is when you predict damage on players. You start your heal before the damage is done.

The more you play the more you'll recognize when people are going to take damage. Healers often hot up tanks even if they're 100% hp because they know they will take damage anyway and the hots will work. There are people who memorize swing timers of bosses so they can pre-cast a healing spells and make sure they land right after the tank takes a big hit. Dragons with flame breath are a good example. You can pre-cast a big heal before the big damage hits. 

Paladins, because of their infinite manabar, dont even really need to calculate swingtimers as they can just precast all the time without worrying about their mana and overhealing. Druids are very hot-based so it makes sense for them to pre-hot tanks and maybe even other players if they expect incoming damage. 

My advice is try to learn proactive healing: precasting / renews.

author: Lirya
content:
Once you reach mid-high levels while leveling, it is undeniable that Smite has better dps compared to wanding. If you stack Spirit + Spirit Tap then you also won't oom while spamming Smite so you only do 1-2 Wand shots to finish off the mob. Your by far best dps talent is Divine Fury (20% faster smites) so you 100% need to get that from the Holy Tree. 

Going Spiritual Guidance next is very natural for the Spirit Tap synergy (and you just got Divine Spirit to buff yourself with even more spirit) and you get a couple of nice benefits for healing dungeons on the way, but you can certainly argue going down disc is better. 1-2 points in Piercing Light is really good value, priests are well suited for fighting mobs higher level than us while leveling. Mental Agility is really good, 10% less mana cost has great synergy with mana recovery from Spirit Tap. Better Fortitude/Shields for survivability is okish, Improved Inner Fire is pretty good, and then +12% damage from Purifying Flames is really good (probably better than Spiritual Guidance).

Personally on my farming/grinding spec at 60 I use a 31/15/5 spec cause I value the disorient + instant from Chastise to interrupt a spellcasting mob and +4% crit and damage from FoW higher than Spiritual Guidance, while others might prefer the extra spell damage.

author: HolyScheiss
content:
Sir @Dragunovi , I havent played Twow the past 3-4 months, as I took a break, but the recent rework of all the Smite (Discipline) sets is very well done and thank YOU and the team for that. I just wish we had it earlier!! 😄

I managed to collect a full T3 set and play with it during the last few days on Twow and experience a different rotation and playstyle from the usual Holy Fire/3-4smites.  Thank you for that, it was truly different experience than before with T3 and opening more options : 
I created a talent build for the T3 set bonuses : https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/priest?points=DoACRYaAZIAoB-CoFCABAg-
__Ressurgent Shield really became a viable option with T3 6-set bonus__ to either save yourself, the tank or someone else and **benefit truly** from it.
a) With the 8-set bonus you have the opener :  Chastise -> Holy Fire and then PWS -> 2x Smite -> Holy Fire
You can pump the stacks for Blessed Wildfire or do it another way, **you have options**, you dont need to have a strict rotation, it's more loose and fun! 
I had 5-6k+ crits on Holy Fire (full consumes,buffs,bonuses and effects) - it was slapping hard!!

b) Using the Blessed Wildfire for Holy Nova spam (shield 5 stacks, chastise 10 stacks) is great and adds flavor and multi use of the set bonuses. 
I personally did not like the T3 set as much for AoE spam, as __*I already had items collected for my AoE spam set*__ -> Epic chest from Sunken Temple, Bindings of Magic (K40 bracers), K40 legs and other items that are spell land/hit effects (BoED, WoC).

Unfortunately I needed two more pieces of T3.5 to experience the rotation with the 5-set effect, which looks very strong and *__brilliantly couples Shadow Word Pain in the rotation__*! 
I couldn`t try the T2.5 (5-set bonus) too - how much power level it had compared to Full T3 or the best combo (4x T3, 5x T3.5).

I was lucky enough to get Ring of Holy Light from K40 thrash last year, it was really a godsend and I used it till the very end! ❤️

author: HolyScheiss
content:
I used Pain Spike even as Smite priest as a finisher for thrash (when its not worth to start casting a spell, mob dies in the next <2 seconds)

Spriest was a mana battery in TBC, and making mana pool/usage/regen as a balancing factor would definitely increased the Spriest usability in raids - but of course it will create other potential problems :))) 
Spriest was never intended to do AoE damage - however it is viable to use Holy Nova as Spriest, some had an AoE set for that, others didnt bother to do it - personal preference I guess. Some thrash is better to deal with via single target rather than AoE cleave, but it depends on the raid/instance. 
=> Shadowform changing Holy Nova to Shadow Nova with potential adjustment on spell power scaling or mana cost - would definitely be better than forcing spriests to farm Holy DMG items to deal with thrash 😄 
=> You might argue, well Ele Shaman was the same way like Spriest - yes, it had only fire nova totems & Chain Lightning - but the popcorn was recently introduced (aka Earthquake) and __I would agree with that!__ 

With sufficient time available, the Twow team would have done more iterations and reached a more satisfying version for Spriest - the recent changes with Talents, Skills and Itemization - all were in the right direction.
